name: Pomalidomide + Dexamethasone (Pd)

biomarkers.note: Pomalidomide/dexamethasone is an IMiD-based doublet and is not biomarker-restricted. Pomalidomide retains activity in disease refractory to lenalidomide and/or bortezomib. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Multiple Myeloma, v5.2026.

treatmentSetting: therapy for previously treated (relapsed or refractory) multiple myeloma
lineOfTherapy: previously treated multiple myeloma, typically after prior lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor; also the backbone for pomalidomide-based triplets

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma after at least one prior therapy (commonly after lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v5.2026, MYEL-G (Therapy for Previously Treated Multiple Myeloma; pomalidomide-based regimens after lenalidomide and a PI)

drugs.name: Pomalidomide

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 74, Table 74.6 (Common Treatment Regimens in Multiple Myeloma), p.1520, Pd entry, line 286293 (Pomalidomide 4 mg on days 1-21)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286293). Pomalidomide 4 mg PO on days 1 to 21 of a 28-day cycle. The DeVita text notes the usual dosage is 2 to 4 mg daily on days 1 to 21 every 28 days. Requires VTE thromboprophylaxis and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen).

drugs.name: Dexamethasone

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: Chapter 74, Table 74.6, p.1520, Pd entry, line 286294 (Dexamethasone 40 mg PO on days 1, 8, 15, and 22)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed., Table 74.6, p.1520 (line 286294). Dexamethasone 40 mg PO on days 1, 8, 15, and 22 of a 28-day cycle. A lower weekly dose may be used for older or frail patients; dose taken exactly as the source prints it.

supportiveCare: Pomalidomide: VTE thromboprophylaxis (aspirin for standard risk, anticoagulation for higher risk) and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen). Side effect profile similar to lenalidomide.
Herpes zoster (VZV) prophylaxis and infection surveillance per institutional practice.
Antiemetics: low emetic risk; prophylaxis per emetogenicity tier.

monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets before each cycle

doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume pomalidomide at a reduced dose per labeling for grade 3 to 4 neutropenia; consider G-CSF; clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Chapter 74 (Plasma Cell Neoplasms), Table 74.6, p.1520, Pd entry (lines 286293 to 286295); pomalidomide pharmacology text (usual dose 2 to 4 mg days 1 to 21 every 28 days)

guideline.locator: MYEL-G (Therapy for Previously Treated Multiple Myeloma; pomalidomide-based regimens for disease refractory to lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for Pd (pomalidomide + dexamethasone) in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (#82). Every dose is sourced to DeVita 12th ed., Chapter 74, Table 74.6 (p.1520): pomalidomide 4 mg PO days 1 to 21 (line 286293); dexamethasone 40 mg PO days 1, 8, 15, 22 (line 286294); 28-day cycle. DeVita additionally states the usual pomalidomide dose is 2 to 4 mg daily days 1 to 21 every 28 days. Setting (previously treated disease, activity after lenalidomide/bortezomib refractoriness) is sourced to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Multiple Myeloma v5.2026, MYEL-G. Pomalidomide requires VTE prophylaxis and REMS. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
